narrative.overview:
NileChain’s visual system is a calibrated agri ops console: verdant trust signals on warm paper, bilingual enterprise clarity, and teal reserved strictly for AI provenance. It serves farm-first B2B work—profiles, matches, reliability, and contracts—without drifting into rustic farmhouse nostalgia or neon crypto dashboards.

Density is scan-first Operate UI across Farm, Factory, and Admin shells (fixed 280px sidebar, sticky frosted top bar), with a quieter marketing landing that reuses the same palette and type. Light mode is the default paper world; dark mode flips to a charcoal ops console while keeping the same roles and spacing.

Confirmed visual rejections: purple SaaS gradients, glassmorphism as a product language (legacy `.glass-card` is deprecated), playful consumer agri kitsch, and using provenance teal for CTAs, nav, or success states.
keyCharacteristics: Nile Forest Green as the rare, decisive brand accent on Warm Paper neutrals
Work Sans (Latin) + IBM Plex Sans Arabic (Arabic) with tabular Data figures for scores and money
Tonal surface steps first; soft shadows only for lift and sticky chrome
Logical CSS / RTL-safe shells; Material Symbols for iconography
Provenance Teal as the Reasoning Spine for AI explanation UI only
Contract signing uses a separate contract-paper visual lane (document metaphor), not the default ops surface language

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Nile Forest Green (and its container) owns brand action. Provenance Teal never substitutes for it.

rules.name: The Provenance Lane Rule
rules.body: Teal appears only on AI reasoning / risk-instrument surfaces. If a control is a normal CTA, it is green—not teal.

rules.name: The Contract Paper Lane Rule
rules.body: Contract document UI may use paper-warm fills, muted #5f6b64 meta ink, and paper-specific radii. Do not restyle Operate dashboards to match paper, and do not “fix” paper hexes into forest/ops neutrals.

rules.name: The Data Figures Rule
rules.body: Scores, money, and tonnage use .ui-data* (tabular nums). Do not style decision numbers as ordinary body weight.

rules.name: The Documented Ramp Rule
rules.body: Prefer named Tailwind type steps for feature UI. Shell density rem sizes and contract-paper type are allowed exceptions where they already ship; do not invent parallel ramps for ordinary screens.

rules.name: The Logical Shell Rule
rules.body: New chrome uses logical inset/border properties so EN LTR and AR RTL stay mirrored without one-off physical margins.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: At rest, prefer border + surface step. Introduce shadow-md as a state (hover, drawer, focus elevation), not as default decoration on every panel.

rules.name: The Soft Instrument Rule
rules.body: Cards are xl-rounded paper panels; buttons are lg-rounded (1rem)—not stadium pills except icon-only utilities and badges.

dos: Do drive Operate color through CSS variables (--color-*) so light/dark stay coherent.
Do use primary-container for primary CTAs and reserve solid primary for accents, rails, and focus.
Do render match/reliability/EGP/tons with .ui-data* tabular figures.
Do keep Provenance Teal on AI/risk reasoning chrome only.
Do build shells with logical properties for RTL Arabic.
Do prefer the documented Tailwind type and radius tokens; treat shell intermediates and contract-paper values as named exceptions when matching existing chrome.
donts: Don't use provenance teal for buttons, sidebar active states, or success badges.
Don't revive .glass-card / .glass-panel as the product surface language.
Don't invent purple gradients, neon glows, or rustic farmhouse textures.
Don't hardcode light-only hex in feature SCSS when an Operate token exists.
Don't normalize contract-paper colors/radii into the ops token set just to silence detectors—document the lane instead.
Don't fabricate partner logos or “#1 network” proof as visual system requirements—those are unverified marketing claims, not design tokens.
